label: Wood colour
tooltip: The base colour of the wood. Pick a pale colour for birch or ash, a mid brown for oak, a deep one for walnut. Changes show instantly; the grain is not repainted.

label: Contrast
tooltip: How strongly the wood's surface marks stand out from the base colour: the grain lines, the fine fibres, the brush dabs, the knot and the light along each plank. Lower is soft and washed out, higher is rough and weathered. The carving, cracks, plank edges, gaps and cut ends keep their strength. Changes show instantly.

label: Colour drift
tooltip: How much the colour wanders in soft patches across the planks, like boards cut from different trees. Zero is one even colour, higher is blotchy and patchwork. Changes show instantly.

label: Seed
tooltip: Picks which random wood you get. Each number is a different layout of grain, carving, cracks and plank joints; the same number always gives the same wood. Repaints the tile.

label: Carving strength
tooltip: How strongly the broad carved scoops and raised patches show on the planks. Zero leaves the surface plain, higher makes the patches' edges catch light and shadow more deeply. Repaints the tile.

label: Carving openness
tooltip: How much of each carved patch's outline fades into the plank instead of closing into a loop. Low gives patches with clear, closed outlines; high lets the outlines fade away so the carving blends into the grain. Repaints the tile.

label: Carving count
tooltip: How many carved scoops and raised patches there are on each plank. Zero is none, 1 is the standard hand-worked look, higher covers the planks with more of them. Repaints the tile.

label: Plank gap width
tooltip: How wide the dark joints are, between planks and where a plank is cut across. Small gives tight, well-fitted boards, large gives rough planks with open gaps. Repaints the tile.

label: Grain lines
tooltip: How many long grain lines run down each plank. Fewer gives calm, clean boards, more gives busy wood with lots of streaks; zero leaves the planks without any. On the first and third planks one of these lines is a bold one that runs the whole length of the plank. Repaints the tile.

label: Weakest grain line
tooltip: How strong the faintest grain lines are. Low lets some lines almost disappear, high makes every line clear. Set above the strongest line, it raises that one too. The bold line on the first and third planks does not follow it: the seed gives that line a strength between 1.7 and 2.1. Repaints the tile.

label: Strongest grain line
tooltip: How strong the boldest ordinary grain lines are. Low gives an even, quiet grain, high lets a few lines cut in deeper. Set below the weakest line, it is painted at the weakest line's strength. The bold line on the first and third planks does not follow it: the seed gives that line a strength between 1.7 and 2.1. Repaints the tile.

label: Light along plank
tooltip: How much light pools along the middle of each plank. Higher makes a soft bright patch along each board with the rest slightly darker; zero is flat even lighting. Repaints the tile.

label: Edge highlight
tooltip: How bright the thin line of light along the lit edge of each plank is, like a worn, rounded corner catching the light. Zero is none, higher is a sharper bright line. Plank edge light multiplies it. Repaints the tile.

label: Plank edge light
tooltip: How strongly the edges of each plank facing the light are lit, as if rounded off. Zero leaves the edges flat, higher gives a brighter bevel and a brighter thin line. Scales Edge highlight too. Repaints the tile.

label: Worn edge light
tooltip: On makes the light along the plank edges patchy, as if worn: it comes and goes along the board. Off makes it an even, unbroken line. Repaints the tile.

label: Edge darkening
tooltip: How dark the thin line is right at the edge of each plank, where it meets the gap. Zero is no line, higher outlines every plank in a darker, crisper edge. Repaints the tile.

label: Edge jitter
tooltip: Fine, small jitter on the long edges of the planks. Zero gives ruler-straight boards, higher gives hand-sawn, slightly ragged edges. Repaints the tile.

label: Edge bends
tooltip: Slow, long bends in the long edges of the planks. Zero keeps them straight, higher makes each board gently curve along its length instead of jittering. Repaints the tile.
